entry.title: Release v5.24.0
entry.content:
Release v5.24.0

New Model additions

Inkling 2 Mini

Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is a smaller sibling of Inkling 2 Small, added in v5.23.0. It has 24 decoder layers instead of 48, and compensates with a looping mechanism in which layers 6 to 17 run three times. A learned message-passing mechanism mixes the residuals of the previous pass into the attention and mixture-of-experts inputs of each loop layer. The decoder has a hidden size of 2304 and routes each token to 8 of 128 experts. The image encoder, tokenizer and processor are the same as Inkling 2 Small's.

A research checkpoint (TML-d24-varloop-research) has the same architecture but supports a variable number of loop passes. Fewer passes are faster, and more passes improve quality. Both checkpoints contain NVFP4 and MXFP8 quantized layers, which are dequantized at load time.

Links: Documentation | Blog Post | HF Blog Post

  • Add Inkling2 Mini (#51050) by @guarin

Apertus 1.5

Apertus 1.5 is a multimodal model from the Swiss AI Initiative that accepts text, images and audio and generates text. It extends the Apertus language model with the EMU3.5 vision tokenizer for images and WavTokenizer for audio. The EMU3.5 tokenizer is an image-only VQGAN with the same encoder as Chameleon's, and it assigns codes by the largest inner product with the codebook. The media tokenizers turn images and audio into discrete tokens, which the language backbone processes alongside text in a shared input vocabulary. The output vocabulary contains only text tokens, so image and audio generation are not supported.

Links: Documentation

  • Apertus 1.5: add model (#47662) by @RaphaelKreft

WavTokenizer

WavTokenizer encodes 24 kHz mono audio into discrete tokens using a single codebook, at 40 or 75 tokens per second depending on the checkpoint, and reconstructs audio from those tokens. WavTokenizerModel encodes and decodes, and WavTokenizerEncoderModel only encodes. Speech, music/audio and unified checkpoints are available. The 40-token-per-second variant is the audio tokenizer of Apertus 1.5. Training the codec is not supported.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Apertus 1.5: add model (#47662) by @RaphaelKreft

Dory

Dory is a looped (latent-recurrent) language model from NVIDIA. It uses a normalized-GPT architecture with interleaved sliding-window and full attention layers. A shared block of layers is applied repeatedly, so Dory can spend more compute per token. The loop count can be changed at inference time on the same checkpoint to trade speed against quality.

Links: Documentation | Paper (nGPT)

  • Add Dory model support (#50099) by @shan18

HY4-VL

HY4-VL (Hunyuan V4 Vision-Language) combines the HYV4 mixture-of-experts text backbone with a vision encoder for image-text and video-text generation. It supports dynamic-resolution visual inputs and uses multimodal rotary position embeddings (mRoPE) to represent temporal and spatial positions. It builds on the Qwen2-VL design and shares its vision patch merger with HunYuan-VL.

Links: Documentation

  • Add HY4-VL (#50877) by @vasqu

Omnilingual ASR

Omnilingual ASR is a suite of multilingual speech-recognition models from Meta FAIR that covers more than 1,600 languages. Each model pairs a Wav2Vec2-style audio encoder with one of two heads:

  • CTC (OmniASRForCTC): a linear projection to the vocabulary, decoded non-autoregressively with greedy CTC.
  • Audio language model (OmniASRForConditionalGeneration): audio embeddings are projected into a Llama decoder that generates the transcription. It optionally takes a language code (e.g. "eng_Latn"), which generally improves transcription quality.

Both variants come in 300M, 1B, 3B and 7B sizes.

Links: Documentation | CTC Documentation | Paper

  • Adding Omnilingual ASR models (#43265) by @ebezzam

Lara Mini

Lara Mini is a multilingual base language model from Translated with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters per token. It is a hybrid of linear-time recurrent layers, sliding-window attention and a few global attention layers, each followed by a fine-grained mixture of experts. The weights are released under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license (non-commercial use) in a gated repository.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Add Lara Mini (#50819) by @ValeGian

SarvamMLA

SarvamMLA is the architecture of Sarvam-105B, a 105B-parameter mixture-of-experts language model from Sarvam AI. It combines Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with sparse MoE routing: 128 routed experts with 8 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. It uses sigmoid routing with group-based top-k selection and YaRN rotary embeddings for contexts up to 131K tokens. The architecture is the same as DeepSeek-V3, with a custom configuration.

Links: Documentation

  • Add SarvamMLA model (sarvamai/sarvam-105b) (#44569) by @aashay-sarvam

SarvamMoE

SarvamMoE is the architecture of Sarvam-30B, Sarvam AI's 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model. It uses grouped-query attention with QK normalization, and 128 routed experts with 6 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. The architecture is the same as GLM-4-MoE, so the auto classes load it with the GLM-4-MoE implementation and only SarvamMoEConfig is specific to SarvamMoE.

Links: Documentation

  • Add SarvamMoE (sarvamai/sarvam-30b) (#51023) by @hmellor

EXAONE

EXAONE covers the EXAONE 3.0, EXAONE 3.5 and EXAONE Deep language models from LG AI Research. Their architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load them with LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM, and only ExaoneConfig is specific to EXAONE. The released checkpoints are renamed to the Llama names when loading and back when saving, so they no longer need trust_remote_code=True.

Links: Documentation

  • Add EXAONE (#50966) by @hmellor

Model updates

  • Ling 3.1 Flash now loads natively through BailingHybrid, like Ling 3.0 in v5.20.0 (#49737) by @icavan
  • Beam gains a BeamForTokenClassification head (#50634) by @AymenKallala

Breaking changes

Cache renaming: past_key_values / cache_params → cache (#50585, #50730)

past_key_values and cache_params are renamed to cache across the library. The old names still work with a deprecation warning; see the dedicated section below.

  • 🚨🚨 Rename past_key_values/cache_params to cache (#50585) by @Cyrilvallez
  • Bump minimal peft version for cache name compatibility (#50730) by @Cyrilvallez

Attention models used to call their cache past_key_values, while Mamba-style and linear-attention models called it cache_params. Hybrid models therefore had to juggle two names for the same object. There is now a single name, cache, everywhere: model forward signatures, generate, prepare_inputs_for_generation, the masking utilities, and every ModelOutput.

# Before
outputs = model(input_ids, past_key_values=past_key_values, use_cache=True)
next_cache = outputs.past_key_values

# Now
outputs = model(input_ids, cache=cache, use_cache=True)
next_cache = outputs.cache
  • Fully backward compatible for now: past_key_values= / cache_params= are renamed to cache automatically, with a one-time deprecation warning. Model forward and prepare_inputs_for_generation accept the old names until v5.40.0, and generate accepts them until v6.0.0. Passing both an old name and cache raises a ValueError.
  • Outputs too: outputs.past_key_values, outputs.cache_params and outputs["past_key_values"] still return the cache. Output classes can also still be built with the old field names (e.g. CausalLMOutputWithPast(past_key_values=...)), so most remote-code models keep working unchanged.
  • Custom code: models defined outside the library should rename their arguments to cache. Layers now call cache.update(key_states, value_states, layer_idx, kwargs=kwargs), so custom Cache subclasses that override update should accept the extra kwargs argument.

🚨 peft>=0.22.0 is now required.

📚 Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/kv_cache

Multimodal Outputs

Generative multimodal models now return shared output classes (MultimodalBaseModelOutputWithPast, MultimodalCausalLMOutputWithPast, and their MoE variants) instead of one output class per model. Code that checks for a model-specific output class should switch to these.

  • 🚨 Multimodal Model Output for generative LMs (#50379) by @zucchini-nlp

modeling_attn_mask_utils.py has been removed. Every function in it had been deprecated in favor of transformers.masking_utils. Remote-code models that still import _prepare_4d_causal_attention_mask or AttentionMaskConverter from it must move to transformers.masking_utils.

Other things

  • Remove deprecated and unused older mask API file (#50728) by @Cyrilvallez

LayoutLMv3 (and the PP-DocLayoutV2 reading-order model that shares its code) now go through the attention interface, so SDPA and flex attention are supported. The relative position bias is built once per forward pass and passed to attention as position_bias.

  • 🚨 LayoutLMv3: support SDPA through the attention interface, build the relative position bias once (#50688) by @14H034160212

Cache

Beyond the rename, this release adds static-cache support to assisted decoding and fixes generate with flex attention and a static cache. StaticCache now allocates values with the value states' dtype, and the cache is kept under activation checkpointing when gradients are off. The is_linear / is_croppable properties are fixed for hybrid linear/full-attention models, BigBird block-sparse decoding works with a KV cache, and KV sharing is restored for the Gemma 4 assistants.

  • Support static cache in assisted decoding (#49415) by @jiqing-feng
  • Simplify cache handling in generate (#50910) by @Cyrilvallez
  • Fix generate with flex attention and a static cache (#50864) by @tarekziade
  • Allocate the StaticCache values with the value states' dtype (#49554) by @qgallouedec
  • Keep the cache under activation checkpointing when gradients are off (#50890) by @qgallouedec
  • [cache] Fix is_linear property to correctly remove hybrid layers (#51030) by @Cyrilvallez
  • Fix is_croppable property for mixed linear-full attention classes (#51028) by @Cyrilvallez
  • Fix BigBird block-sparse decoding with a KV cache (#49984) by @jiqing-feng
  • fix(gemma4): Restore KV sharing for the Gemma 4 assistants and their targets (#50531) by @harshaljanjani
  • Fix Dory vocabulary resizing, loop validation, and last-loop static caching (#50982) by @shan18
  • Fix device placement in test_bc_cache_name_{forward,generate} (#50757) by @ydshieh
  • Update test_dynamic_cache_hard expected values for A10G (#50822) by @ydshieh

Generation

Generation fixes cover sampled beam search (candidates are sorted again before finalization), constrained sampling (batch IDs are preserved), generate on MPS with encoder-decoder models, and TextStreamer, which no longer drops spaces or lags on text without spaces such as Chinese, Japanese and Korean. StopStringCriteria initializes faster, and its cache now actually hits.

  • Fix long lagging when streaming text without spaces and NJK chars (#36708) by @CNSeniorious000

Continuous batching

Continuous batching now works under torch.inference_mode() and finds sharded key/value projections under any decoder path. The per-token memory estimate scales with the TP size, warmup handles async and static inputs correctly, and an out-of-bounds error in the top-k processor is fixed.

Chat templates, parsing and serving

Chat parsing gets a new python-call-list content parser, better handling of bare keys and duplicate XML arguments, and three further parser fixes. apply_chat_template accepts message objects, and assistant masks are correct with left truncation. transformers serve handles a missing Hub cache, lists loaded models in /v1/models, keeps local paths containing @, and keeps assistant content when tool_calls is empty.

Pipelines

Multimodal pipelines now accept media-only inputs and string assistant prefills, keep Mistral prefills in Voxtral, stop mutating generation kwargs, and return chat messages as input_text when returning tensors. pipeline also respects a device_map that targets a single device.

Vision

Vision fixes cover Muse Glimmer's embedding order, GotOCR2 and Emu3 image sizes, Kimi video inputs, NemotronH Omni video forwarding, SAM3 RoPE precision in bf16, and DETR-family configs with dilation=None. SigLIP2 and LFM2-VL now process all images at once with tensor ops. Flash Attention is turned off for multimodal models whose image mask it would drop.

Audio

Audio fixes cover the OmniASR CTC blank token, Qwen3 Omni audio kwargs, Qwen3-ASR's truncation=False default, PeAudioVideo loading with timm 1.0.31, and the audio training examples.

entry.title: Release v5.23.0
entry.content:
Release v5.23.0

New Model additions

Inkling2

Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch.

Links: Documentation | Blog Post

  • Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in #50682

JEV

JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. JevForDecision is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (head.safetensors and judge_config.json for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental decision pipeline or directly with decide.

LFM3

LFM3 is the third generation of Liquid Foundation Models from Liquid AI. Like LFM2, it is a hybrid architecture that combines gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention, with the attention layers split between full-attention and sliding-window layers. The attention layers apply RMSNorm to the query and key heads and gate their output with a per-head sigmoid. Every layer applies a sandwich norm to the operator and feed-forward outputs before the residual addition.

LFM3-VL

LFM3-VL is a vision-language model family from Liquid AI, built on the LFM3 language model. It takes images and videos at their native resolution together with text. It combines a hybrid vision encoder (a linear patchifier, gated depthwise 2D convolution layers, and bidirectional grouped-query attention layers with 2D rotary embeddings) with a projector and an LFM3 language model. The projector merges each 2x2 block of patch features into one language token through a layer norm and a two-layer MLP.

Exporters: export, share and run any model on its backend (#50029, #50032, #50309, #50311)

exporters.mp4

Every export now returns an ExportedModel. You call it like the original model (same kwargs, same output class), push it to the Hub, and load it back on the backend's own runtime. The same API covers Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch.

from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.exporters import ExportedModel, OnnxConfig, OnnxExporter

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2")
inputs = tokenizer(["Exporters are here!"], return_tensors="pt")

exported = OnnxExporter().export(model, inputs, OnnxConfig(dynamic=True, ort_fusions="cuda"))
exported.push_to_hub("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx")

exported_model = ExportedModel.from_pretrained("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx", device="cuda")
outputs = exported_model(**inputs)  # same output class as model(**inputs)
  • Fused for the runtime: OnnxConfig(ort_fusions="cpu" | "cuda" | "webgpu" | "dml") rewrites the graph into ONNX Runtime's fused transformer ops at export time: attention, GroupQueryAttention over the KV cache, rotary, norms and MoE. OpenVINO exports now hit OpenVINO's fused CPU kernels for attention, RoPE, MoE experts and compressed int8/int4 weights, which makes decode 2.4–3.9× faster than before.
  • Faster than torch.compile: on EmbeddingGemma2 (8 × 128 tokens), ONNX Runtime with the TensorRT EP is 7.6× faster than eager PyTorch and 1.4× faster than torch.compile on an A100. OpenVINO is 4.1× faster than eager and 2.2× faster than torch.compile on a Xeon Platinum 8570 (4.9× and 2.6× with int8 weights).
  • Shareable: an export saves and loads like a model, optionally in a subfolder of the model repo. Its export.json records the config, input shapes, package versions and I/O names. Quantized exports (PT2E, NNCF, ONNX Runtime) save and run the same way.

🚨 export() returns an ExportedModel, and an ONNX program is an onnx_ir.Model. OnnxConfig's and OpenVINOConfig's output_path options are gone in favour of save_pretrained. Custom backends register with register_backend.

📚 Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/exporters

entry.title: v5.22.0: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)
entry.content:
New Models

Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)

Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe.

Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union.

Key Features

Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices:

  • ~1T total / ~52B active parameters: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert.
  • 1M context length, for long-context workloads.
  • Multimodal input: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios.
  • Instruct and Reasoning functionalities with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request.

Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities:

  • Reasoning Mode: three reasoning efforts — low, medium, high (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run.
  • Vision: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights.
  • Multilingual: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union.
  • System Prompt: strong adherence and support for system prompts.
  • Agentic: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement.
  • Cybersecurity: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests.
  • Large Context Window: supports a 1M context window.

The model is released under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License: a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral.

Recommended Settings

  • Reasoning Effort:
    • 'low' / 'medium' / 'high' — default is 'high'.
    • Use reasoning_effort="high" for complex prompts and agentic usage, 'low' for fast chat replies and 'medium' for day to day usage.
  • Sampling: for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters:
    • temperature=1.0
    • top_p=0.95
  • System Prompt: define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems.
  • Tools: keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case.
  • Context: the checkpoint supports a 1M context window.

Breaking changes

  • 🚨 Separate EP logic into its own file (#49679) by @3outeille

Quantization

FP8 quantized models can now be used for adapter training (such as LoRA with PEFT). Backward passes were added to the dense and grouped FP8 matmuls, and is_trainable is now True. Backward also dequantizes experts in chunks and skips autograd at inference, which cuts peak memory in the MoE layer backward from about 28.9 GiB to 2.8 GiB at 8k tokens. Separately, the AMD CI image now install

entry.title: Release: v5.21.0
entry.content:
Release v5.21.0

New Model additions

MiniCPM-OCR

MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Feat test (#49920) by @guarin in #49920

Flint

Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense.

Links: Documentation

  • Add Flint model support. (#49824) by @lovishmadaan in #49824

UltraVBert

UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The max_image_tiles setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page.

Links: Documentation

  • Add UltraVBERT (#49685) by @athrael-soju in #49685

Gradium Phonon TTS

Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. A causal transformer reads a voice prompt and the text, then emits one continuous 32-dimensional audio latent per step at 12.5 Hz through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when the utterance ends. The latents are decoded to 24 kHz audio by a Pocket TTS audio tokenizer. Unlike Pocket TTS, voice conditioning uses 512-dimensional latents from a separate, unreleased speaker codec, so voices come as precomputed latents and cannot be cloned from a recording.

Links: Documentation

  • Add GradiumPhononTTS (#49791) by @eustlb in #49791

Pocket TTS

Pocket TTS is Kyutai's 100M-parameter text-to-speech model, built as a Continuous Audio Language Model that runs faster than real time on CPU. A causal transformer emits one continuous audio latent per frame (12.5 Hz) through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when to stop. A Mimi-based audio tokenizer encodes voice prompts and decodes the generated latents to 24 kHz audio. Two flow heads are released, Lagrangian self-distillation (default) and drifting, and voices can be cloned from a recording, passed as precomputed latents, or loaded from cached KV states.

Links: Documentation | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (the Continuous Audio Language Models paper, arXiv 2509.06926). It is the only paper the documentation links, and it describes the architecture family Pocket TTS belongs to. The docs do not cite a separate Pocket TTS technical report.) | [Blog Post](NONE. The documentation links no official blog post. It points only to the original code repository at https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts.)

  • add PocketTTS (#49589) by @eustlb in #49589

Pocket TTS Audio Tokenizer

The Pocket TTS audio tokenizer is the codec used by Pocket TTS. It has Mimi's architecture (SEANet convolutions plus a small causal transformer on each side), but its residual vector quantizer is replaced by a continuous 32-dimensional bottleneck, the VAE-GAN from Continuous Audio Language Models. It converts 24 kHz audio into latents at 12.5 Hz and decodes them back to audio. It serves as the audio_tokenizer of PocketTTSProcessor, encoding voice prompts and decoding generated latents, and its encoder and decoder can also be loaded on their own.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • add PocketTTSAudioTokenizer (#49588) by @eustlb in #49588

Breaking changes

Fixed Gemma4 processor imports (the Gemma4, Gemma4 unified and EmbeddingGemma2 processors) so from transformers import * no longer fails in environments that have PIL but not torch; no user action is needed.

  • 🚨 Fix gemma4 cross imports resulting in import failing without torch but with PIL (#49748) by @Sai-Suraj-27

Added an "fp8" backend to QuantizedCache, alongside quanto and hqq, that stores KV states in torch.float8_e4m3fn with a single scale per tensor; enable it with cache_implementation="quantized" and cache_config={"backend": "fp8"}.

  • 🚨Add an FP8 backend to QuantizedCache (#48677) by @jiqing-feng

Tensor parallelism now has a dedicated embedding style, shards every model's input embeddings by default, and supports widths that aren't divisible by the TP size, so ColwiseParallel and RowwiseParallel now apply only to linear layers; custom TP plans that applied them to embeddings must switch to the new embedding style.

  • 🚨 TP: give embeddings their own style, shard input embeddings by default, and shard widths that don't divide by the TP size (#49570) by @IlyasMoutawwakil

Every MoE TP and EP plan now shards its experts, so models no longer keep all experts on every rank, and a new test_moe_parallel_plans_shard_experts test enforces this; custom or downstream MoE parallel plans must add expert sharding to pass it and to avoid wasted memory.

  • 🚨 MoE: shard the experts in every TP/EP plan, and test for it (#49206) by @IlyasMoutawwakil

Cache

This release improves cache handling across the library. Flash Attention now works with static caches, BLOOM no longer crashes with static cache or compiled generate, chunked prefill supports cache continuation, and the Qwen4-Exp indexer's position history stays aligned with its cached keys. Linear-attention caches also gain new getters (is_recording_past, get_recurrent_state, conv-state access) that stop exposing cache internals and prepare for paged-c

  • [FA] Fix FA with static cache (#49998) by @Cyrilvallez in [#49998]

entry.title: Release v5.20.0
entry.content:
Release v5.20.0

New Model additions

Muse Spark Open

Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats.

Links: Documentation | Blog Post

  • Add Muse Spark Open (#49644) by @guarin in #49644

Ling 3.0

Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as BailingHybridForCausalLM, so it loads without trust_remote_code=True.

Links: Documentation

  • [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support (#49446) by @icavan in #49446

Kolibri1

Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers.

Links: Documentation

  • Add Kolibri 1 (#49463) by @lucamotz in #49463

MiniCPM-V 4.7

MiniCPM-V is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by OpenBMB. Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes.

The main addition over 4.6 is canvas M-RoPE: instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a (temporal, height, width) position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order.

  • Fix more stuff (#48979) by @zucchini-nlp in #48979

UnlimitedOcr

UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Add Unlimited OCR (#46836) by @guarin in #46836

UltraBERT

UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings.

Links: Documentation | Paper

  • Integrate the UltraBERT architecture (#49596) by @tomaarsen in #49596

MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize

MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as [start][S01]text[end]. It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages.

Links: Documentation

  • Add MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize model (#48386) by @itazap in #48386

Breaking changes

🚨 General breaking notice that inference with EP has regressions in speed; we are working on fixing this ASAP! 🚨

Deprecated checks and methods have been removed from cache_utils.py (affecting models such as minimax_m3_vl and pi0), so any code still calling those deprecated cache methods must switch to the current cache API.

  • 🚨 Remove deprecated cache utils methods (#49605) by @guarin

Accidental imports from other models were removed from several model files (e.g. embedding_gemma2, ijepa, lightglue), and the modular converter now avoids adding such cross-model imports. If you imported these names through those model modules, import them from their original modules instead.

  • 🚨 Remove imports from other models (#49473) by @guarin

The minimum kernels version is now 0.17.2, which allows use_fallback=KernelizeFallback.ALL so that a failed kernel load falls back to the original implementation instead of raising an error. Upgrade kernels to 0.17.2 or later.

  • 🚨 Bump min kernels to 0.17.2 for better fallback (#49235) by @SunMarc

A new SubConfigSpec centralizes the initialization of sub-configs, so default sub-configs are collected from dataclass fields instead of by instantiating the class, and this touches the configuration utilities and many model configs. Custom or existing nested configs may need to be updated to declare their sub-configs through this mechanism.

  • 🚨 SubConfigSpec for centralized init of subconfigs (#48282) by @zucchini-nlp

The LUKE and mLUKE tokenizers now treat entity special tokens such as <ent> as special tokens (not split, honored by skip_special_tokens, normalized) while keeping the same spacing as regular vocabulary tokens when decoding. Tokenization and decoding output involving these tokens may therefore differ from before, so check any code or saved outputs that depend on the old behavior.

  • 🚨🚨🚨 luke fixe (#48408) by @itazap

Exporters

Transformers exporters now support quantization directly during export across Dynamo, ONNX, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch. The new unified quantization API integrates PT2E, ONNX Runtime, and NNCF quantizers, enabling static and dynamic quantization as well as weight-only compression (INT8/INT4), with configurable calibration workflows. This makes it easier to export optimized models for efficient inference across different backends.

For more information see the docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/exporters_quantization

Parallelization

This release improves distributed training and inference. FSDP × TP model and optimizer checkpoints can now be saved and loaded across different parallel configurations, and expert-parallel dispatch, tensor-parallel plans, static-cache generate(), and the caching allocator's byte count were fixed. Tied LM heads in composite models now get their own TP plan entry, enable_expert_parallel applies the EP plan alone again, TPU loading uses the `tor
